## Description

Programme: MDV-P1-E12 · UX programme: safe, cohesive clinic workspace (from the Nov 2026 product UX audit). Track D (design rules and UI component setup), wave D3. No audit backlog id. Created from the audit's rulings and blueprint, not from a backlog line (see Findings).

Persona and route: /patients/:id (patient record), the schedule appointment panel, the prescription table at narrow widths · doctor, receptionist.
Findings and reviewers: No consolidated finding number. Reviewer findings B-17, B-21, and the prescription table part of B-04 and C-10, which the audit's backlog did not turn into a ticket. Found while checking every reviewer finding against the tickets.
Rationale: The patient record is 3,241 to 5,129 px tall and the doctor scrolls past six Not recorded tiles to reach the medicines; its pinned filter takes 156 px of a phone. A completed visit's panel shows four disabled actions with the same reason four times. The prescription table needs 1,000 px and scrolls sideways inside itself from 768 to 1023 px, hiding dose columns.
Proposed UX behaviour: Patient record: an empty section collapses to one line with its add action (Vitals: none recorded · Add); the filter chips are one sideways-scrolling row of 52 px; link buttons align to the text edge. Appointment panel: for a completed visit the four actions are replaced by one line, This visit is completed. Prescription lines from 768 to 1023 px render as stacked rows (medicine, dose, frequency, duration each visible) and never scroll sideways inside the table. Unknown values stay Not recorded in words; nothing is guessed or hidden.
Prototype and blueprint reference: None. Reviewer B, screen-by-screen critique.
Components and tokens affected: Card, Chip, the Table stacked variant when the table ticket has landed (before that, a local stacked layout for the prescription lines).
Front end and back end split: Front end only.
Prerequisites and blocked by: Blocked by the page components and chip tickets. Timing: after the first pilot weeks, or before the first staff training session if the founder moves it there; never between training and the first two pilot weeks (arbitration ruling 6).
Clinical sign-off: Ask the pilot doctor in passing whether collapsed empty sections hide anything they rely on; not a merge gate. Not recorded must still be visible as words for allergies in every case.
Effort and regression risk: M · Low. The allergy state is never collapsed.
Deliberately NOT in this ticket: (1) Changing section order on the patient record. (2) The patient record's life-stage modules.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1.** Given a patient with six empty sections at 1440 by 900, when the record opens, then each empty section is one line with its add action and the medicines start within the first two viewports
- [ ] **AC2.** Given allergies not recorded, when the record renders, then the allergy block is shown in full with its words
- [ ] **AC3.** Given 375 px, when the record scrolls, then the pinned filter is at most 56 px tall
- [ ] **AC4.** Given a completed visit's panel, when it opens, then one line says the visit is completed and no disabled button repeats a reason
- [ ] **AC5.** Given a prescription with three lines at 768 px, when it renders, then dose, frequency and duration of every line are visible with no sideways scrolling
- [ ] **AC6.** Given English and Arabic, when axe runs, then there is no violation
